NOODLRHOOKS.Capabilities.Hint: When a scene loads, hand each creature's written abilities — Regeneration, Pack Tactics, a monster's own Multiattack — to the Noodlr module, which asks an AI to turn them into rules this module can actually run. Each distinct wording is read once and then remembered forever, so a scene of twenty goblins costs one reading. It needs Noodlr installed and configured with your own AI provider key, and it spends a little of that credit the first time it meets an ability, which is why it is off until you ask for it. With it off, everything else in this module works exactly as before.

NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoDamage.Hint: The 5e system works out whether an attack hit inside the chat card it draws and then stores the answer nowhere, so it has nothing to act on: what it gives you instead is an Apply button, once per target, for every hit at the table. With this on, a hit's damage lands on the creature it was rolled against — resistance, vulnerability, immunity and temporary hit points all resolved by the system itself, never recalculated here — and a whispered receipt tells you what moved, with an undo. This is also what switches on the rules that hang off damage: death saves, dropping to Unconscious at zero, instant death, and the concentration save. Where the answer is genuinely unclear — no readable AC, a target the record cannot identify, or a spell whose saving throws have not been rolled yet — nothing is applied, the Apply button is left exactly where it is, and you are told why.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoDamage.Manual: Damage not applied automatically — {why}. Use the Apply button on the damage card.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoDamage.Name: Apply rolled damage without the button
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoDamage.Why.NeedsS: this one is decided by a saving throw, and resolving saves is switched off
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoDamage.Why.NoActi: the roll did not come from an item, so there is nothing to say who it was aimed at
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoDamage.Why.NoAtta: no attack roll was recorded for it, so whether it hit is not known here
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoDamage.Why.NoHitP: that sheet has no hit points to change

NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoDamage.Why.Update: the sheet could not be updated — see the console

NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Gate.Title.Graze: Missed. Graze has already dealt the flat damage; the weapon's dice do not apply.

NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.DamageGate.Hint: The 5e system draws Attack and Damage side by side and leaves both live from the moment the card appears, because it has no verdict to hold the second one on — it decides whether an attack hit inside the card's renderer and stores that answer nowhere. So the two commonest mistakes at a table are the ones the card invites: rolling damage on a miss, and rolling it twice because the first press produced nothing visible. With this on, Damage stays locked until the attack has been rolled and the reaction window has closed — a Shield cast in that gap turns a hit into a miss — then turns green, and takes one press. A miss keeps it shut; a Graze weapon pays out its flat damage without it. Nothing here can strand you: an unreadable card, no GM connected, or simply no answer within thirty seconds all hand the button back, and you can unlock any card by hand.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.DamageGate.Name: Hold the Damage button until the attack is settled
NOODLRHOOKS.CompactCards.Hint: Draw the system's activity and roll cards at roughly half their usual height. Text stays the same size — what goes is the padding, the gaps and the repeated portraits. Affects only your own screen.
NOODLRHOOKS.CompactCards.Name: Compact chat cards
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoSaves.Hint: The 5e system rolls a saving throw against the right DC and then compares it to nothing: the result is a number in chat, and a person works out half of 24. With this on, a save is joined back to the spell that demanded it and settles the damage — half, none, or the full amount, whichever that spell says a success is worth — with the system resolving resistance and Evasion as usual. Creatures nobody but you can roll for roll their own saves the moment the spell is used, so a fireball on five goblins costs you no presses at all. Characters with a player owner are left alone, because that player came to the table to roll their own dice. A Paralyzed or Unconscious creature that auto-fails Strength or Dexterity is treated as having failed — the Apply button should not wait on a roll that was correctly cancelled. What a failed save inflicts beyond damage — Restrained, Prone, and the rest — is not applied: that is written as prose on the item, and guessing at it would start an argument.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoSaves.Name: Let saving throws settle the damage
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoSaves.Why.NoActiv: that damage was rolled without its usage card, so there is nothing to match the saves against
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.LegendaryResistance.H: The 5e system already draws a "Resist" button on a failed monster save and waits for someone to notice it. That worked while you were also applying the damage by hand — the same pause served both — but a save that now rolls itself and settles its own damage in one breath leaves that button on a card whose consequences have already happened. With this on, you are asked instead, on a six-second clock, before anything lands. You are only asked where it changes something worth changing: a failure that does anything other than damage, or damage that is a real share of what the creature has left. A lich is not asked about a Firebolt. If the clock runs out the creature takes it, because three resistances a day is the most depleting resource in the game and no timer should spend one for you.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.LegendaryResistance.N: Offer a legendary resistance on a failed save
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoRecharge.Name: Roll rechargeable abilities at the start of a monster's turn
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoRecharge.Hint: A breath weapon, a gaze, a swallow — anything marked Recharge 5–6 — spends its use and then waits for a d6 at the start of that monster's next turn. The 5e system can roll that die and ships the switch off, hidden under Combat Settings → Monsters, so a spent breath stays spent for the rest of the fight and the planner correctly stops offering it. That looks like the monster forgot it can breathe. This is that switch, on this page, defaulting to automatic without a chat card: the die is not a fun roll, and a table of eight dragons should not dump eight cards. Announce posts the system's recharge card. Off leaves it for a human. If you already turned dnd5e's Auto-recharge on, that one wins and this stands aside so the die is not rolled twice.
NOODLRHOOKS.Legendary.StakeEffect: and what that costs it is not damage
NOODLRHOOKS.Legendary.TakeHint: the save stands as rolled — this is what happens if the clock runs out
NOODLRHOOKS.Legendary.Title: Legendary Resistance
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.ReactionPrompts.Hint: A reaction is the one resource in the game that is lost by not noticing it, and nothing in the 5e system tells anybody theirs has come up: no prompt when a creature steps out of your reach, none when something hurts you off-turn, and no "when you are hit" moment at all, which is why Shield has never worked without Midi QoL. With this on, the creature's own reaction options are offered to whoever plays it — the player who owns the sheet, or you for a monster — on a six-second clock, once per round, and the thing chosen is rolled on that person's own client. What the clock is allowed to pick by itself is fixed and deliberately narrow: a free swing with the weapon already in hand, yes, because an unused reaction is gone at the end of the round anyway; a spell slot or a limited use, never, whatever the clock says. Creatures Noodlr is playing for you are not asked — they have a planner to decide — so this never becomes a queue of dialogs about goblins. Counterspell has its own switch below, because it works by pausing somebody else's cast rather than by answering something that has already happened. Silvery Barbs is still not offered: it needs a d20 somebody else rolled to be taken back, and an offer that cannot be honoured spends the slot and changes nothing.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.ReactionPrompts.Name: Offer a reaction when one comes up
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Counterspell.Hint: Counterspell is the reaction spellcasters most expect to work and the one that never has: catching a cast means noticing it in the half-second before the damage card appears, so in practice it is played by asking the table to rewind. With this on, a spell with Verbal, Somatic or Material components is held for a moment when an opposed creature within 60 feet can see it, holds Counterspell and still has its reaction — everyone else's casts are untouched, and nothing is held when no such creature exists. At most two are asked, on the same six-second clock, and the clock never spends the slot for them. The 2024 rules are what make this honest: the caster makes a Constitution save against the counterspeller's spell save DC, and a countered spell costs the action but not the slot, which is exactly what happens when the cast is stopped before the system charges for it. A boss can spend a legendary resistance to push through. Split by the caster, so you can leave your monsters' spells uninterruptible and still let the party's be countered.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Counterspell.Name: Hold a cast open for Counterspell
NOODLRHOOKS.Counterspell.Casting: {name} begins casting {spell} — holding for a moment in case anyone counters.
NOODLRHOOKS.Counterspell.Countered: {counter} counters {name}'s {spell}. The spell dissipates with no effect, and the slot is not expended.
NOODLRHOOKS.Counterspell.Name: Counterspell
NOODLRHOOKS.Counterspell.Resisted: {name} holds against {counter}'s Counterspell. {spell} goes off as cast.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Barbs.Hint: Silvery Barbs, and every other reaction that spoils a roll somebody has already made. The spell is famously hard to run at the table because the die is on screen and the consequence follows immediately, so playing it means asking everyone to hold on. With this on, a made saving throw and a landing attack are held for a moment when an opposed creature within 60 feet can see the roller, holds the spell and still has its reaction; the d20 is rerolled and the lower result kept, which the card then shows the way it shows any roll made with disadvantage. Only the reroll is automated — the ally who gains Advantage is whatever your copy of the spell carries as an effect, because that is a promise about a roll nobody has made yet. The clock never casts it for anybody: it is a slot spent on a gamble, since the fresh die may be higher and the roll stands anyway. Ability checks are not offered, because nothing here holds a check's verdict open — a check produces information rather than a consequence. Split by whoever rolled well, so you can leave your monsters spoilable and the party alone.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Barbs.Name: Hold a success open for Silvery Barbs
NOODLRHOOKS.Barbs.Held: {caster} twists {name}'s luck — {was} becomes {rolled}, for {total}. Not enough: it still stands.
NOODLRHOOKS.Barbs.Name: Silvery Barbs
NOODLRHOOKS.Barbs.Spoiled: {caster} twists {name}'s luck — {was} becomes {rolled}, for {total}. The roll no longer succeeds.
NOODLRHOOKS.Barbs.Unrolled: {caster} casts against {name}, but the die could not be rerolled. The roll stands.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Sneak.Hint: Sneak Attack, which the system rolls perfectly well and nobody remembers to press. The dice were never the problem: the feature is on the sheet with the right formula for the rogue's level. What is missing is that the button is equally pressable on a turn where none of the conditions hold, and that after a good attack roll the table has already moved on. With this on, a hit is read for you — a finesse or ranged weapon, and either Advantage on the roll or one of your allies standing within 5 feet of the target while you have no Disadvantage — and if it qualifies, whoever plays the rogue is offered it on a six-second clock. The dice are rolled on that person's own client, so the animation and the card are theirs, and the damage lands down the same path as everything else, with an undo on the card. Once per turn, tracked in and out of combat, and pressing the feature from the sheet yourself counts, so you are never asked twice for one turn. Taking it is the default when the clock runs out, because an unused Sneak Attack is simply gone. Split by the rogue, so you can run the party by hand and still have the bandits' work done for you.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Sneak.Name: Offer Sneak Attack when a hit qualifies
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Sneak.Title: Sneak Attack — {name}
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Sneak.Ally: You hit {target}, and one of your allies is within 5 feet of it.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Sneak.DealHint: rolled on your own sheet — this is what happens if the clock runs out
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Sneak.HoldHint: no extra damage, and it is still yours this turn
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Ready.Hint: The Ready action, which every table knows and almost nobody uses, because a held action is a promise nothing keeps track of. With this on, pressing Ready asks what you are waiting for and what you will do about it, spends your Action now, and then watches the round for you — movement, damage, a creature dropping, a spell being cast, an attack, a condition landing, something coming into view, a door, the end of a turn, and anything the GM narrates. When it happens you are asked to confirm on a six-second clock, and the clock fires it, because you already said this is what you wanted; aborting is the deliberate choice and costs you the Action and nothing else. Releasing spends your Reaction, so a readied Attack is one attack — Extra Attack needs the Attack action on your own turn. If nothing triggers it before your next turn, it is lost. If Noodlr's AI game master module is installed you can write the trigger in your own words ("if a goblin I can see approaches an ally, I shoot it") and it will be read for you; without it, you pick from a short list of the common ones, which is also what monsters use. One divergence from the letter of the rules, in your favour: a readied spell spends its slot when it goes off rather than when you declare it, so a trigger that never comes costs you the Action only.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Ready.Name: Hold an action for a trigger you name
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.AbortHint: you lose the readied action and nothing else
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Aborted: {name} lets the moment pass, and the readied action with it.
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Expired: {name}'s readied {action} is lost — the trigger never came.
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Explain: Say what you are waiting for. You will then be asked to click the action you are holding, from your own sheet.
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Gone: {name} cannot use {action} any more, so the readied action is lost.
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Lost: {name} cannot take a reaction, so the readied action is lost.
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.MoveInstead: Hold movement instead of an action
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Moves: {name}'s readied movement is released — move now, out of turn.
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.NoAction: {name} has no action left to ready with.
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.NoCompiler: no module is installed that can read a trigger written in words

NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.NoTrigger: Nothing was readied: a held action needs a trigger.
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.PickAction: Now click the action you are holding, on your own sheet.
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Prose: Your trigger, in your own words
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.ProseHint: If a goblin I can see approaches an ally, I shoot it
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.SpellNote: Held spells spend their slot when released, not now.
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Title: Ready an action
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.TooSimple: {name} is not clever enough to lie in wait for something.
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Understood: Read as: {summary}. Is that what you meant?
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Unwatchable: That trigger cannot be watched for — {why}.
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Trigger.Casts: An enemy starts casting a spell
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Trigger.Leaves: An enemy backs out of my reach
NOODLRHOOKS.Ready.Trigger.Reach: An enemy comes within my reach
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoEnd.Hint: End the encounter automatically once no hostile creature is left standing, instead of handing out turns to an initiative order in which nobody has an enemy. The summary card is posted either way.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoEnd.Name: Clear the tracker when the fight is won
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoEngage.Failed: Noodlr spotted the party for a hostile creature but could not start combat — see the console. Automatic engagement is paused for a minute.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoEngage.Hint: Every six seconds, checks whether any hostile creature can actually see a player's token — through that creature's own vision, senses and the walls between them, not through your view — and if one can, adds everyone on the scene to the encounter, rolls initiative for the monsters and waits for your players to roll their own before the fight actually begins. If nobody rolls within a minute, the rest is rolled for them so the table is never stuck. Applies only while Combat Automation is Full or Partial. There is a one-minute lull after each fight ends, so survivors who still have the party in sight cannot immediately start the next one. Turn this off for ambushes and set-piece openings you want to time yourself.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoEngage.Name: Hostile creatures start the fight themselves
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoEngage.RolledFor: Nobody rolled in time, so initiative was rolled for the rest of the party and the fight begins.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutoEngage.Surprised: caught completely unawares — Disadvantage on initiative.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Automation.Hint: Who plays the monsters. Full: Noodlr takes every non-player creature's turn as it comes up. Partial: only the creatures you hand it, by selecting a token and pressing the Act-as-NPC tool — press it again to take one back mid-fight. Off: nothing is automated and the tool is hidden. Player characters are never played, in any mode.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Automation.Name: Combat automation
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Automation.Partial: Partial — only the creatures you hand it
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.AutomationOn: Noodlr will play {names} for the rest of this fight.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Concentration.Hint: D&D 5e works out the right DC when a concentrating creature takes damage and whispers a button to its owner — and then nothing reads the answer. No part of the system ends concentration when that save fails; the card shows the failure in red and the spell stays up. With this on, the save is rolled automatically on the client that owns the creature (so a character's save is still the player's own roll, with the usual dialog), a failure ends the spell and says so in chat, and being Incapacitated, dying, or dropping to 0 hit points ends it with no save at all — which is written in the rules and enforced nowhere. There is no undo, because ending concentration also removes whatever the spell had placed on the battlefield and that cannot be faithfully rebuilt. Stands aside when midi-qol's concentration handling is set to anything but None.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Concentration.Name: Roll concentration saves, and end the spell on a failure
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Conditions.Hint: Stock D&D 5e applies statuses and never reads most of them when a roll is built. Poisoned is listed under attack disadvantage and ignored; advantage against a Blinded or Restrained target, disadvantage when you are Blinded or Frightened, auto-fail Strength and Dexterity saves while Paralyzed, Stunned, Petrified or Unconscious, and critical hits within 5 feet of a Paralyzed or Unconscious creature all live only as journal prose. With this on, those rules land on the roll itself, and an Incapacitated creature cannot start an action, bonus action or reaction. Automated turns skip a creature that cannot act (Incapacitated, or Paralyzed / Stunned / Unconscious / Petrified) whether this switch is on or not.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Conditions.Incapacita: {name} is Incapacitated and cannot take that action.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Conditions.Name: Apply condition combat math
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Dying.Failure: {name} takes damage while dying and fails {add} death saving throw(s) ({failures}/3).
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Dying.FirstAid: {healer} steadies {name}'s breathing — Medicine {total} against DC {dc}. They are Stable, but still Unconscious.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Dying.FirstAidFailed: {healer} cannot find the wound in time — Medicine {total} against DC {dc}.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Dying.FirstAidNoTarge: Target the dying creature you want to help first.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Dying.FirstAidUnexpec: Administering first aid could not be completed. See the console for what went wrong.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Dying.Hint: Stock D&D 5e floors hit points at zero and never applies Unconscious, Dead, or death-save failures from damage — instant death when leftover damage meets your hit point maximum is journal prose only. With this on, characters (and Important NPCs) fall Unconscious and start dying, ordinary NPCs are marked Dead and defeated, further damage at 0 adds death-save failures (two on a critical), massive damage kills outright, and healing above 0 clears the marks. Stands aside when midi-qol's Add Dead is enabled. Every card carries an undo.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Dying.Important.Hint: NPCs with the Important trait (the same flag that shows death-save boxes on their sheet) fall Unconscious at 0 like player characters, instead of dying outright. Turn this off if every NPC should drop dead at 0.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Dying.Important.Name: Important NPCs use death saves
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Dying.Name: Apply dying and death at 0 HP
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Dying.Unconscious: {name} drops to 0 hit points and falls Unconscious.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Economy.Ask: {name} has already used {spent} of {max} this turn, and {activity} needs another {slot}. Some features do grant one — Haste, among others — so this may well be legitimate. Continue anyway? Your answer will be posted to the chat log either way.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Economy.Hint: Neither Foundry nor the D&D 5e system counts actions: the only per-turn limits either enforces are legendary actions and movement, so nothing stops anyone attacking five times. This counts an action, a bonus action and a reaction per creature, refreshing at the start of that creature's own turn. Extra Attack and Multiattack are read from the sheet, so a fighter still gets every swing. Creatures Noodlr plays are always held to this exactly, whatever you choose here.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Economy.Logged: {name} used {activity} with no {slot} remaining, at {user}'s election.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Economy.Name: Hold players to one action per turn
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Economy.Off: Don't count — Foundry's usual honour system
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Economy.Title: That's more than one turn's worth
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.EngageRadius.Hint: When a hostile creature spots the party, only other hostiles within this distance of it join the fight — the rest of the map carries on unaware. Measured in the scene's own units, through walls, since this is a shout. Set to 0 and the creature that spotted you fights alone.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.EngageRadius.Name: How far a creature can call for help
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Forced.Hint: Nothing in the stack does this. The 5e system automates no forced movement at all — no activity type has a field that could hold a distance, the Push weapon mastery is a tooltip, and every distance in the published content sits in description prose. Repelling Blast ships as an enchantment that appends ", Repelling" to the cantrip's name as a reminder for you. With this on, a shove, a Push-mastery hit, Thunderwave, Thorn Whip, Repelling Blast, Crusher and the rest move the creature: away, toward, or straight up. Walls, occupied spaces and the map's edge all stop it, hazards it lands in are called out, and every card carries an undo.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Forced.Lifted: {name} is thrown {distance} {units} into the air by {cause}.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Forced.Name: Make pushes and pulls actually move the target
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Forced.Restored: Returned {count} creature(s) to where they stood.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Hide.Hidden: slips out of sight — anyone searching needs a Perception check of {dc} or better to find them.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Hide.NoSelection: Select the token that wants to hide first.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Hide.Unexpected: The Hide action could not be completed. See the console for what went wrong.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.InvisBreak.Hint: The Invisibility spell ends the moment its target makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell, and nothing in Foundry enforces that — the break condition is written only in the spell's description. Greater Invisibility is deliberately left alone, because not ending is the entire reason it costs a fourth-level slot. Potions and innate invisibility are untouched. This is separate from hiding on purpose; the two are different states and are switched separately.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.InvisBreak.Name: End Invisibility when its target attacks

NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Movement.Hint: Nothing else enforces this. Foundry records how far a token has moved on its turn and the 5e system colours the drag ruler red once you pass your Speed, but neither ever stops you, so a character can cross the whole map and still act. With this on, the token stops at the edge of its Speed — and a character with something left to spend may keep going, which is charged as a Dash and said out loud in chat. Rogues, monks and anyone under Expeditious Retreat are charged a bonus action rather than their action, as their features intend. The GM's own dragging is never restricted.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Movement.Name: Hold creatures to their Speed
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Movement.Spent: {name} has already moved {spent} of {max} {units} this turn.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.MoveSpeed.Hint: How fast an automated creature slides across the canvas. A creature that arrives instantly reads as a teleport rather than a walk, and players notice. 0 keeps Foundry's own animation pace; lower numbers make the walk easier to follow. Turns wait for the slide to finish, so a slow setting lengthens turns and may want a longer turn pace above.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.MoveSpeed.Name: Automated movement speed (squares per second)
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.NoPlan: Noodlr found nothing {name} could do — no usable attacks, items, or reachable targets on its sheet.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Pace.Hint: Minimum time an automated creature's turn occupies the table before initiative advances. A machine resolves a turn in under a second, which reads as a blur and makes spoken lines from consecutive creatures overlap. Time already spent acting counts toward this, so it slows only the turns that were too fast. 0 disables it.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Pace.Name: Automated turn pace (seconds)
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.RepeatSaves.Hint: Hundreds of effects say the target "can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success" — and nothing in Foundry or the 5e system rolls it. An effect carries a duration and a status and has nowhere to record a save that ends it early, so a Hold Person or a paralysing bite runs its full length unless somebody at the table remembers the DC every single round. With this on, the save is rolled automatically when the creature's turn ends, on the client that owns it, and a success removes the condition and says so in chat. Clauses come from creature abilities compiled by the companion module, and from the console for anything applied by hand. An effect that midi-qol is already counting down is left alone.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.RepeatSaves.Name: Roll "save ends" at the end of each turn

NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Resolution.Mercy: has spared the party and is now Neutral. The party forfeits its carried currency, held weapons, and worn armour, and gains no experience for this encounter — collected once the last hostile stands down.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Resolution.Over: No hostile creature is still fighting — every one is dead, fled, surrendered, or has stood down. End the encounter when you are ready.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Resolution.Restored: Restored the forfeited gear to {restored} character(s).

NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.SelectToken: Select the token (or tokens) first — Noodlr acts on what you have selected on the canvas.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Stealth.Hint: Before a creature raises the alarm, its passive Perception is checked against the Stealth of whoever it is looking at. Only creatures that have actually taken the Hide action get that contest — the Hiding condition on the token is what counts, whether it came from the Hide button, from Cunning Action, or from ticking the icon by hand. Simply having rolled Stealth does nothing, and hiding ends the moment you attack, cast a spell out loud, or are found. Invisibility and the Ethereal Plane are respected too. Turn this off to go back to pure line of sight.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.HideAlways.Hint: Pressing Hide always rolls and always sticks. Whatever you rolled becomes the number an enemy has to beat to notice you, and anything already looking straight at you simply starts out having noticed — so hiding in plain sight of a guard costs you the action and buys you nothing from that guard, while still hiding you from everyone further down the corridor. The card the table sees never says who noticed or how many, so a hide gives away nothing about who is out there; you get that in a whisper. Turn this off for the printed 2024 rule instead, which refuses the action outright unless you are Heavily Obscured or behind three-quarters cover, out of every enemy's line of sight, and beat DC 15 — bear in mind that a refusal has to explain itself, so it tells the player there is something watching them.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.HideAlways.Name: Always let a creature try to hide
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Stealth.Name: Let hiding keep you unnoticed
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Surprise.Hint: When a fight starts, any hostile creature that cannot see a single member of the party is marked Surprised. Under the 2024 rules the D&D 5e system already turns that condition into Disadvantage on the initiative roll — it simply never decides who deserves it, so nobody ever gets it. Players are never marked automatically: Noodlr only ever asks what monsters can see, so it has no honest way to say a character was unaware. Ambushing the party stays your call.
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.Surprise.Name: Mark creatures caught unawares as Surprised
NOODLRHOOKS.Combat.ToggleAutomation: Noodlr: hand this creature to Noodlr (or take it back)
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Influence.Ask: {name} is being asked, by way of {approach}. How does it feel about that?
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Influence.Asking: Waiting for the GM to say how that lands…
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Influence.FailureRea: and fails, rolling {total} against DC {dc}. That approach is closed for a day.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Influence.Hint: The rules give the Influence action a real DC — 15, or the creature's Intelligence score if that is higher — say that a Friendly creature is swayed with Advantage and a Hostile one with Disadvantage, and shut an approach off for 24 hours after it fails. The 5e system lists all three of those rules in its glossary and reads none of them. With this on, you are asked the one question software cannot answer — whether the creature is willing, hesitant, or unwilling — and everything after your answer is worked out and rolled: the right skill on the right sheet, with the right Advantage, against the right DC, and remembered afterwards so nobody talks the same guard round eleven times. A willing creature simply agrees and an unwilling one simply refuses, with no dice either way.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Influence.Locked: {name} has already turned down that approach ({approach}) today.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Influence.Name: Roll the Influence action against a real DC
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Influence.NoGM: No GM is connected, and only the GM can say how the creature takes it.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Influence.NoTarget: Target the creature you are trying to influence first.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Influence.Title: How does it take that?
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Influence.Unexpected: The Influence action could not be completed. See the console for what went wrong.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Influence.UnwillingR: — and it refuses outright. No check, and no bar on asking again another way.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Influence.WillingRea: — and it agrees, in the way it prefers. No check needed.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Auras.Hint: A Paladin's Aura of Protection — and Courage, Devotion, Warding, Aura of Life — should add their bonus to every ally within the moving radius. dnd5e never does that: the feature's Active Effect stays on the Paladin, and clicking it posts the prose. Importers stamp flags for Active Auras or Aura Effects; with those modules off the stamp does nothing. This copies a resolved number (the Paladin's Charisma, not the ally's) onto whoever is in range, and skips the Paladin when the sheet already transfers the bonus onto them so it is not applied twice. Distance is rechecked every six seconds (one combat round), so walking away drops the bonus even if the Paladin stands still. The Paladin and nearby allies see the aura's own icon on their tokens, beside concentration and conditions, without replacing those. Stands aside when Aura Effects or Active Auras is running, so two copies cannot stack. DAE alone does not emanate and is not a reason to stand aside.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Auras.Name: Creature auras apply to allies in range
NOODLRHOOKS.General.TransformUndo.Name: Restore a transformation from the token
NOODLRHOOKS.General.TransformUndo.Hint: While Wild Shaped, Polymorphed or Shapechanged, the token shows a restore icon in the same corner as a Paladin's aura badge. Clicking it calls dnd5e's own Restore Transformation — it does not spend a Wild Shape use, and it does not intercept Argon's Wild Shape button, so beast-to-beast still works. The click is handled as a token click (Foundry does not deliver pointer events to effect sprites). The Token HUD also gets a restore control. The system's sheet header and sidebar remain.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.TransformUndo.NoOwne: You do not own that creature, so you cannot restore its form.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.Name: Creatures can mount and ride tokens
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.Hint: A creature may mount a willing creature at least one size larger that shares its disposition or is Neutral (player characters may also mount Friendly). How many fit is the mount's grid space (half its token squares — a Large horse seats two Medium riders; a Gargantuan dinosaur seats a party) plus remaining carry weight. Mounting or dismounting during your move costs half Speed, rounded down. Riders follow the mount and cannot walk independently — click the saddle icon or the Token HUD to dismount. Every six seconds, and whenever the mount changes size, each rider is checked against that capacity; anyone who no longer fits falls off without spending Speed. Stands aside when Rideable is active. A controlled mount's initiative matches the first rider; restricting it to Dash, Disengage and Dodge, and falling-off saves, are not in this first slice. The 2024 rule does not grant a free Dash.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.Rideable: Rideable is handling mounts in this world.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.NoSelection: Select the token that wants to mount or dismount first.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.AlreadyRiding: That creature is already mounted. Dismount first.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.Occupied: That mount does not have room for another rider.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.Loop: That would make two creatures ride each other.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.Size: A mount must be at least one size larger.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.Disposition: That creature will not carry them.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.Carrying: That mount cannot carry this much weight.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.TooFar: Move next to the mount first.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.Speed: Mounting costs half Speed, and this creature has none left to spend.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.WalkFirst: Dismount before walking on your own. Click the saddle icon.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Riding.FellOff: {rider} falls from {mount} — it can no longer carry them.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.InteractReach.Hint: Opening or closing a door requires a token within one square of it. Arm's Reach can look like it already does this, and at its default it does not — every GM click is unrestricted, including a GM who is playing a character and clicks from across the map. With this on, a distant click is refused and says so. A GM with no token selected is staging and is not restricted. A player with no token on the scene cannot reach a door.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.InteractReach.Name: Doors only open from within reach
NOODLRHOOKS.General.InteractReach.NoToke: Select the token that is opening that door first.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.InteractReach.TooFar: That door is out of reach.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Jump.Hint: A Long Jump carries you a number of feet up to your Strength score with a 10-foot run-up, and half that from standing; a High Jump is 3 feet plus your Strength modifier, again halved from standing. Foundry has a jump movement action and the 5e system prices it correctly, but nothing anywhere limits how far one leap goes — so jumping is currently a way to cross difficult terrain for free, with no upper bound at all. With this on, a leap that goes further than the creature could clear is refused and says why, counting the run-up it has actually taken this turn. The distance still comes out of that turn's movement, as the rules say it should. The GM is never restricted.
NOODLRHOOKS.General.Jump.Name: Hold a leap to the distance it could clear
